headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: Airflow can egress broadly while awesome-python has no runtime protections or runnable surface, so the pair is mostly inert but not fully risk-free.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between airflow and awesome-python. Airflow has broad network egress, but awesome-python has no runnable surface or input parser, so there is no plausible default prompt-injection bridge in the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Do not route Airflow outputs into any parser that treats text as instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow can egress broadly, but the profiles show no data classes touched and awesome-python has no runtime or outbound capability. That makes leakage possible only if operators place sensitive files into Airflow and then expose them through a new bridge; the pair itself does not show a default leak path.
conditions: IF sensitive data is introduced into Airflow and a new export path to awesome-python is configured, leakage becomes possible.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets or regulated data in Airflow tasks.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on any future export path.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is marked runnable false and awesome-python is a non-runnable source-available collection, so there is no overlapping write surface, OAuth scope, or mutable shared resource in the profiles. The pairwise conflict pathway is therefore blocked by the documented surfaces.
conditions: IF either profile is later deployed as a writable service against the same directory or database, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: Keep both agents non-runnable in this deployment.
Do not grant shared write access to any directory or database.
Review any future OAuth scopes before enabling them.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow does not have a documented downstream action-taking role here, and awesome-python is only a repository of links, not an executor. With no runnable behavior or authoritative output chain between them, there is no default cascade from one agent's output into the other's actions.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs are later consumed as authoritative inputs by a separate executor, cascading error risk should be reassessed.
mitigations: Require human review before any downstream action.
Do not treat repository content as operational truth.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before automation.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data class mismatch is documented for either airflow or awesome-python. Because both profiles lack touched data classes and compliance metadata, there is no evidenced compliance pathway to score beyond none.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data with distinct residency or retention rules, compliance risk must be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Add retention and residency policies if regulated data is introduced.
requires-engineering: map future compliance controls to the data flow.
